nodes.summary: Strips separators and uppercases a container number into canonical ISO 6346 form.

nodes.name: validateContainerFormat
nodes.summary: Checks the owner code and serial portions of a container number against ISO 6346 letter/digit regexes.

nodes.name: calculateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Computes the ISO 6346 check digit using the letter-to-number map and powers-of-2 weighting with modulo-11 reduction.

nodes.name: validateCheckDigit
nodes.summary: Verifies that a container number's trailing digit matches its computed ISO 6346 check digit.

nodes.name: validateContainerNumber
nodes.summary: Full validation pipeline combining normalization, format checks, and check-digit verification for a container number.

nodes.name: suggestCorrections
nodes.summary: Searches the space of single-character fixes (digit and owner-code letter substitutions) for container numbers whose check digit fails, ranking candidates by edit distance.

nodes.name: tripDriverSalary.ts

tour.title: Project Overview & Repository Shape
tour.description: Start with CONTEXT.md, the repository's own orientation document: it defines which sources are authoritative and how the codebase is organized, which matters in a project where conventions are recorded in docs rather than a root README. Together with pnpm-workspace.yaml you can see the three-package monorepo shape — backend, frontend, and a shared contracts package — that every later step fits into. Notice the domain up front: this is a Vietnamese trucking logistics platform (trips, shipments, containers, VND financials) deployed as TingTing for the SilverSea customer.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point
tour.description: backend/src/index.ts is the runtime bootstrap with the highest fan-out in the graph (40 direct imports): it wires telemetry, Express 5, the Casbin enforcer, the Drizzle database client, and Redis, then mounts every API router and starts the job scheduler. Read it as a table of contents for the backend — each import is a subsystem you will visit in the next steps. The deliberate initialization order (config, DB, auth, then routes) is the pattern to notice.
tour.languageLesson: Express 5 apps are assembled by registering middleware in order before mounting routers — order is semantics here: auth/Casbin middleware must wrap the route tree so every handler runs inside an authenticated, authorized context.

tour.title: Shared Contracts & Financial Calculations
tour.description: The shared package is the platform's contract layer and its most-imported dependency (fan-in 254): shared/src/index.ts re-exports the domain vocabulary, while schemas/index.ts holds 107 Zod schemas used for validation on both server and client. The calculations module is the financial heart — round.ts provides round2dp, the canonical rounding rule behind VND amounts, and tripTotals.ts is the core P&L engine computing fuel, revenue, and cost per trip. Every money figure you see later in billing and ledger services flows through these pure functions, which is why they are exhaustively unit-tested in place.
tour.languageLesson: Zod acts as a single source of truth: `z.infer<typeof TripSchema>` derives the TypeScript type from the runtime schema, so the API request shape, the validation logic, and the client types can never drift apart.

tour.title: Database Schema & Persistence
tour.description: These are the two most-depended-upon files in the entire codebase (fan-in 334 and 333): schema.ts is the canonical Drizzle schema with roughly 170 table exports, application-owned enums, checks, and a custom pgvector type, while db/index.ts exposes the singleton postgres.js client every service queries through. The generated baseline migration (0000_flexible-baseline.sql, with per-table nodes) shows how the ~124-table Postgres database is actually created. Key domain tables to locate: shipments, trips, dispatch_handoffs, billing_documents, ledger, and customers — they back every service in the steps ahead.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle defines the schema as typed TypeScript objects and generates SQL migrations from them — code-first schema authoring. The project rule is strict: Drizzle ORM only, no hand-written raw SQL in application code.

tour.title: Authentication & Casbin RBAC
tour.description: Every request passes through two gates: middleware/auth.ts verifies the JWT bearer token against a Redis blacklist and loads the user with role and customer scope, then middleware/casbin.ts translates the HTTP method into a Casbin action (read/write/delete) against route-scoped resources. The enforcer in casbin/enforcer.ts loads model.conf and policy.csv at boot — the policy file is where the five roles (ADMIN, DISPATCHER, CLERK, ACCOUNTANT, FORWARDER) get their route-by-route permissions. This is the mechanism behind the role-gated pages you will see in the frontend, and the backend's fan-in numbers (79 and 47) confirm nearly every route depends on it.
tour.languageLesson: Casbin policies are triples — subject (role), object (route resource), action — evaluated by the model's matcher. One repo-specific pitfall worth remembering: requireRoles REPLACES the role set rather than extending it, so stacking it accidentally locks out admins.

tour.title: Domain Core: Shipments, Dispatch & Trips
tour.description: This is the operational heart of the order-to-cash flow, one BFS hop from the entry point. shipment.service.ts handles shipment CRUD with idempotent create and status transitions; dispatch-planning.service.ts (about 2,500 lines) is the dispatch engine managing handoffs, queues, fleet listings, and order issuance to trips with resource-availability checks; and trip-status-machine.service.ts governs the trip lifecycle states. trip-shared.ts is included because its Tx transaction type alias is the foundation all trip services share — the pattern to notice is services cooperating inside one Drizzle transaction rather than calling each other loosely.

tour.title: Finance: Billing, Ledger & Governance
tour.description: When trips complete, money flows through three cooperating engines. billingDocument.service.ts (about 4,300 lines) generates debit-note drafts with VAT snapshots and version tokens; ledger.service.ts posts double-entry-style trip-completion and reversal entries that collect payables and receivables; and adjustment-governance.service.ts (the highest fan-out service in the graph) implements the approval workflow for AR adjustments, financial closes, and completed-trip cancellations. The financial/index.ts router mounts all finance sub-routers in a deliberate order, mirroring how these services are composed. All amounts here are computed with the round2dp/tripTotals helpers from Step 3 and persisted into the ledger and billing_documents tables from Step 4.

tour.title: AI Agent, LLM & Scheduler
tour.description: The backend hosts a multi-lane AI assistant: agent/orchestrator.ts routes user intent to specialized lanes (FAQ fast lane with pgvector embeddings, financial overview, deterministic reports, lookups), backed by an LLM provider registry and a tool registry the BFS shows fanning out into domain-specific tools. The assistant streams to the frontend over agentSocket.ts, a dedicated socket channel separate from the REST API. The scheduler (registry + runner) runs recurring jobs such as GPS capture and receivable reminders on durable-effect infrastructure, so learners should see this subsystem as async work layered on top of the synchronous route/service core.

tour.title: Frontend Entry & App Shell
tour.description: Crossing to the frontend: main.tsx mounts the React 19 app inside StrictMode with TanStack Query and BrowserRouter (plus a stale-chunk self-heal handler for zero-downtime deploys), and App.tsx composes the global provider stack — auth, toast, agent directives, month, search, reduced motion — then defines AppRoutes, a role-gated React Router tree that lazy-loads roughly 80 pages. useAuth.tsx is the client-side half of Step 5's auth story: it fetches and caches the current user, handles login/logout with token revocation, and gates rendering on authentication state. Read App.tsx as the frontend's equivalent of the backend index.ts — a map of everything that follows.
tour.languageLesson: React.lazy + Suspense per route gives automatic code splitting — each page ships as its own chunk, which is why the app installs a stale-chunk self-heal handler: after a deploy, a navigating user may request an old chunk, and the handler recovers by reloading.

tour.title: Client Libraries, UI Kit & Design System
tour.description: Four high fan-in modules are the shared plumbing of every page. lib/api is the typed fetch client with error classes carrying Vietnamese Zod message translations; api/keys.ts is the centralized TanStack Query key factory giving every domain hierarchical, frozen cache keys; components/UI.tsx is the hand-rolled kit (KPI, PageHeader, Panel, Modal, Drawer, Btn) consumed by nearly every page (fan-in 100); and design-system/index.ts is the vendored Untitled UI layer of data tables, tabs, and field components. The layering rule to internalize: pages compose feature modules, features compose UI.tsx and the design system, and all data flows through lib/api with query keys from keys.ts.

tour.title: Feature Deep-Dive: Dispatch Planning Workspace
tour.description: The dispatch workspace is the best tour of the frontend's feature-module pattern, and it consumes the backend engine from Step 6. dispatchPlanningClient.ts is the typed API client for dispatch endpoints; the master plan (useDispatchMasterPlan.ts + MasterPlanGrid) shows handoffs and queue state at a glance, while the detailed plan (useDispatchDetailPlan.ts, with PlateAssignmentCell) supports per-trip plate and carrier assignment. ShipmentsPage.tsx and the clerk's ClerkShipmentCreatePage.tsx complete the intake side of the O2C flow — a shipment created here enters dispatch planning, gets issued to a trip, and eventually becomes the billing documents of Step 7. Note how each feature keeps its hook, grid, styles, and co-located tests together in one folder.

tour.title: Testing, Seeding & Deployment
tour.description: The closing step covers how the platform is verified and shipped. backend/src/seed.ts drives the demo/staging seed suite (250+ Vitest test files live under backend/src/tests, including q23-direct-money-idempotency.test.ts, which shows how carefully direct-money mutations are guarded). The backend Dockerfile is a two-stage build — a node:22-alpine builder compiles TypeScript, then a minimal runtime stage ships only the dist output plus Casbin policy files and Drizzle migrations — and deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml orchestrates the production stack (pgvector Postgres, Redis, backend, nginx-served frontend) for the vantai.tingting.vip deployment documented in docs/deployment.md. This is the capstone: schema (Step 4) becomes migrations, services (Steps 6-7) become tested containers, and the Makefiles tie build, push, and deploy together.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds keep images small by separating build and runtime dependencies; in compose stacks, `depends_on` with healthchecks orders startup (backend waits for Postgres health) and named volumes persist database state across redeploys.
